decisions.quote: We have uncovered some important new results, particularly in respect of gender and stages of economic and political development, but also found support for well-established empirical features of self-employment, around formal and informal human capital. Time and context do matter, even in a world where some things don’t change too much.
decisions.reason: The authors explicitly frame their replication and extension of Cowling (2000) across time and European countries as mixed, confirming established formal and informal human capital relationships while finding changed dynamics for gender and stages of economic and political development (with Hypothesis 4 rejected in earlier waves and supported in later waves).

parent_objection: The first mixed verdict relies on important new results and H4 New-Europe/Old-Europe temporal differences. But source says the original Cowling2000 studied15wealthy WesternEuropean countries; H4 may be an extension absent from that original. The conclusions separately say original core human-capital/age/gender findings are supported; diminished gender gap is magnitude alone. Inspect actual original-versus-current comparisons to determine whether any retested original finding is explicitly presented as not supported,or whether original outcomes are successful and new hypotheses are extensions. Do not infer mixed from new interesting results,smaller gender effects,or confirmation/rejection of an extension H4 across survey waves. Follow authors overall verdict/scope. If supported,explain any original finding that actually differs.

blind_target.title: Are entrepreneurs different across countries?
blind_target.evidence_quote: In the context of the replication we directly replicate the Cowling (2000) study which was set in 1990s Europe, and our study will provide new evidence on the dynamics of self-employment over the next 20 years in the originally studied ‘old’ Europe. But it will also set these dynamics against those apparent in the ‘new’ Europe. And all these dynamics will be set in the unique contexts of some huge social and economic events that have occurred in Europe of the last generation.
blind_target.outcome_quote: We have uncovered some important new results, particularly in respect of gender and stages of economic and political development, but also found support for well-established empirical features of self-employment, around formal and informal human capital.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Conclusion supports the established human-capital features tested in the replication. Gender and development yield new findings, but the authors do not explicitly frame these as replication failures. Verdict is less certain because the conclusion does not name Cowling directly.
